concepts.name: Climatic Threshold Conditions for Tropical Evergreen Forests
key_dimensions: Minimum annual rainfall requirement (>200 cm) and its exceptions in Western Ghats vs Andaman Islands
Temperature range (above 22°C mean annual) and absence of dry season as defining criteria
Humidity threshold (>70%) and its role in distinguishing evergreen from semi-evergreen forests
UPSC trap: Distinguishing between rainfall thresholds for evergreen vs deciduous — overlap zone between 100–200 cm rainfall

concepts.name: Geographical Distribution of Tropical Evergreen Forests in India
key_dimensions: Three primary zones: Western Ghats (windward slopes), Northeast India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya), and Andaman & Nicobar Islands
Absence in peninsular plateau and Deccan — reasons linked to rain shadow effect
Altitudinal limit on Western Ghats (below ~1500 m) vs montane evergreen above that level
UPSC trap: Odisha and Andhra Pradesh coastal strips sometimes cited — understanding why they are semi-evergreen not true evergreen

concepts.name: Stratification and Canopy Structure of Tropical Evergreen Forests
key_dimensions: Multi-tiered vertical structure: emergent layer, upper canopy, middle layer, shrub layer, ground layer
Closed canopy causing near-total light interception — implications for undergrowth density
Epiphytes, lianas, and climbers as structural indicators of true evergreen forest
Comparison with tropical deciduous forests which lack the dense epiphyte layer

concepts.name: Characteristic Flora: Trees of Tropical Evergreen Forests
key_dimensions: Key species: Rosewood (Dalbergia latifolia), Ebony (Diospyros ebenum), Mahogany, Ironwood (Mesua ferrea), Hopea, Dipterocarpus
Northeast-specific species: Rubber (Hevea brasiliensis naturalized), Bamboo dominance in Assam
Andaman-specific species: Andaman Padauk (Pterocarpus dalbergioides), Gurjan — species unique to island ecosystem
UPSC trap: Teak is NOT found in evergreen forests — it is the flagship of tropical moist deciduous forests; confusion frequently tested

concepts.name: Absence of Seasonal Leaf Shedding: The Evergreen Mechanism
key_dimensions: Leaves shed and replaced continuously — no synchronised dormancy unlike deciduous forests
Physiological basis: No moisture stress or cold stress to trigger uniform leaf fall
Economic implication: No 'bare season' — forest floor always covered, affecting soil moisture retention
UPSC trap: 'Evergreen' does not mean individual trees never shed leaves — they do, but asynchronously

concepts.name: Tropical Evergreen vs Tropical Semi-Evergreen Forests: Boundary and Overlap
key_dimensions: Semi-evergreen forests occur where rainfall is 150–200 cm — transitional zone between evergreen and moist deciduous
Semi-evergreen has a mix of evergreen and deciduous species; top canopy may be deciduous
Champion & Seth classification: Semi-evergreen as a distinct type (2B) vs true evergreen (1A, 1B, 1C)
UPSC trap: Questions often conflate semi-evergreen with evergreen — key differentiator is the deciduous element in the upper canopy

concepts.name: Champion and Seth Forest Classification of Tropical Evergreen Forests
key_dimensions: Champion & Seth (1968) classified Indian forests into 16 major groups — Tropical Wet Evergreen is Group 1
Sub-types: 1A (Andaman Tropical Evergreen), 1B (West Coast Tropical Evergreen), 1C (Assam Tropical Evergreen)
Distinction between littoral/swamp forests (Mangroves — Group 4) which are also evergreen but classified separately
UPSC trap: Champion & Seth classification is the official basis — FSI's classification in State of Forest Reports uses different categories; confusion between the two systems

concepts.name: Economic Importance and Commercially Valuable Timber Species
key_dimensions: High-value hardwoods: Ebony, Rosewood, Ironwood — premium international market value
Difficulty of commercial exploitation: Dense canopy, lack of roads, mixed species composition make selective logging hard
Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs): Cane, bamboo (Northeast), resins, medicinal plants
UPSC angle: Why tropical evergreen forests are 'commercially less exploited' despite rich biodiversity — linked to accessibility and mixed species problem

concepts.name: Biodiversity Hotspots and Endemism in Indian Tropical Evergreen Forests
key_dimensions: Western Ghats identified as one of 36 global biodiversity hotspots (Myers et al.) — evergreen forests are the core ecosystem
Northeast India part of Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot — highest plant diversity in India
High endemism: Over 1600 endemic plant species in Western Ghats alone
UPSC trap: Andaman & Nicobar Islands are a separate biodiversity hotspot — distinct from Western Ghats; sometimes confused in MCQs

concepts.name: Soil Characteristics Associated with Tropical Evergreen Forests
key_dimensions: Laterite and lateritic soils dominate Western Ghats under evergreen cover
High rainfall causes intense leaching — soils are nutrient-poor despite dense vegetation (nutrients locked in biomass)
Thick humus layer from rapid decomposition in hot-humid conditions
UPSC trap: Despite dense forest, the underlying soil is NOT fertile for agriculture — this is the 'green desert' paradox frequently asked

concepts.name: Threats and Degradation of Tropical Evergreen Forests in India
key_dimensions: Western Ghats: Plantation monocultures (tea, coffee, rubber) replacing native evergreen forests
Northeast India: Jhum cultivation (shifting agriculture) causing forest fragmentation
Infrastructure development: Linear projects (roads, railways) fragmenting wildlife corridors in evergreen zones
UPSC angle: Kasturirangan Committee report on Western Ghats — Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA) demarcation directly linked to protecting evergreen forests

concepts.name: Tropical Evergreen Forests and Carbon Sequestration
key_dimensions: Dense biomass = highest above-ground carbon stock among Indian forest types
Role in India's NDC commitments: Creating additional carbon sink of 2.5–3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030
REDD+ mechanism (UN) applicable to evergreen forests — India's participation
UPSC angle: Deforestation of evergreen forests = double loss: biodiversity + carbon sink; frequently linked to climate change questions

concepts.name: Western Ghats Evergreen Forests: Specific Characteristics and Sub-Zones
key_dimensions: Windward (western) slopes receive >250 cm rainfall — true evergreen; leeward (eastern) slopes are semi-evergreen/deciduous
Shola forests: A specific type of tropical montane evergreen forest found above 1500 m in Nilgiris and Palani Hills
Shola-grassland mosaic: Unique alternating pattern — shola in valleys, grassland on slopes; fire-mediated ecology
UPSC trap: Shola forests are montane evergreen NOT tropical evergreen — altitude is the differentiator; frequently confused

concepts.name: Northeast India Evergreen Forests: Distinct Features from Western Ghats
key_dimensions: Influenced by both Indian monsoon and Bay of Bengal — highest rainfall in Cherrapunji-Mawsynram belt
Bamboo dominance in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh — bamboo acts as undergrowth in evergreen canopy
Species overlap with Southeast Asian forests (Dipterocarp species) — phytogeographic link to Indo-Malayan region
UPSC trap: Rainfall in Meghalaya is highest globally yet forests are not uniform evergreen — local topography creates rain shadows within the state

concepts.name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands Evergreen Forests: Island Biogeography Dimensions
key_dimensions: Andaman group: Tropical evergreen with species like Gurjan, Andaman Padauk, Chuglam, Marble Wood
Nicobar group: Closer floristically to Malayan forests than Indian mainland — biogeographic isolation
Island biogeography effect: High endemism but lower total species diversity than mainland evergreen zones
UPSC trap: Nicobar Islands' forests are biogeographically distinct from Andaman Islands' forests — both are 'evergreen' but differ in species composition significantly

concepts.name: Relationship Between Tropical Evergreen Forests and Tribal Communities
key_dimensions: Scheduled Tribes dependent on NTFP collection from evergreen forests — Forest Rights Act 2006 implications
Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) like Jarawas, Sentinelese (Andaman), Birhor (Jharkhand) linked to evergreen ecosystems
Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK) held by these communities for forest management
UPSC angle: Tension between conservation (Protected Area buffer zones) and tribal forest rights — Supreme Court cases on eviction from forest lands

concepts.name: Protected Areas and Conservation Frameworks for Tropical Evergreen Forests
key_dimensions: Key Protected Areas: Silent Valley National Park (Kerala) — 'last pristine tropical evergreen forest' in Western Ghats
Namdapha National Park (Arunachal Pradesh) — largest protected area in Northeast covering evergreen forests
UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Western Ghats (2012) — 39 serial properties covering evergreen core zones
UPSC trap: Silent Valley was the centre of a major conservation controversy in 1970s–80s (hydroelectric project opposed by scientists) — this historical controversy is frequently tested

concepts.name: Phenology and Ecological Processes Specific to Tropical Evergreen Forests
key_dimensions: Mast fruiting: Irregular large-scale synchronised fruiting events (e.g., Dipterocarpus) — ecological significance for seed dispersers
Nutrient cycling: Extremely rapid decomposition due to heat and humidity — tight nutrient cycling with minimal leakage
Pollination ecology: High dependence on insects, birds, and bats for pollination — loss of pollinators = forest regeneration failure
UPSC angle: Why clearing evergreen forest and replanting fails — mycorrhizal networks and ecological processes cannot be easily restored; relevant to compensatory afforestation debates

concepts.name: Comparison of Tropical Evergreen and Tropical Moist Deciduous Forests
key_dimensions: Rainfall: Evergreen >200 cm; Moist Deciduous 100–200 cm — rainfall is the primary differentiator
Flagship species: Evergreen = Rosewood, Ebony, Ironwood; Deciduous = Teak, Sal, Shisham — UPSC frequently tests species-to-forest-type matching
Commercial exploitation: Deciduous forests MORE commercially exploited due to single dominant species and seasonal accessibility
Geographical overlap: 150–200 cm rainfall zone supports either type depending on local soil and topography — this ambiguity is a UPSC trap zone

concepts.name: Impact of Climate Change on Tropical Evergreen Forests of India
key_dimensions: Phenological shifts: Changes in flowering and fruiting timing disrupting animal-plant mutualism
Range shifts: Some evergreen species moving to higher altitudes ('uphill migration') — compressing montane zones
Increased fire frequency in forest margins due to prolonged dry spells — unusual for evergreen zones historically fire-resistant
UPSC angle: IPCC reports and India-specific assessments predict 'savannization' risk in transitional zones — conversion of moist forests to drier types; policy implications for NDCs
